Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays and CT scans demonstrate bilateral, peripheral pulmonary infiltrates (often described as a "photographic negative of pulmonary edema"), which is the hallmark radiographic finding of chronic eosinophilic pneumonia. This condition typically presents with persistent opacities that resolve gradually with corticosteroid treatment, distinguishing it from the rapid resolution of acute eosinophilic pneumonia or the transient migratory infiltrates of Churg-Strauss syndrome.
